summary.text: Photosynthesis is how autotrophic organisms with photopigments, such as most plants, algae and cyanobacteria, turn light energy into chemical energy.
The usual kind releases oxygen as a byproduct of splitting water, and it helps produce and maintain the oxygen in Earth's atmosphere.
It happens in two stages: light reactions capture light energy to make NADPH and ATP, and light-independent reactions use them to capture and reduce carbon dioxide.

facts.label: Global energy capture
facts.value: About 130 terawatts, roughly eight times human power use

facts.label: Carbon into biomass
facts.value: Around 100 to 115 billion tons each year

facts.label: Plant pigments
facts.value: Chlorophylls, held inside chloroplasts in leaf cells

facts.label: Relation to respiration
facts.value: In outline, it is the opposite of cellular respiration

items.prompt: People once might have thought a plant lives on soil and water alone. What did Jan Ingenhousz show that it also needs?

options.label: Constant contact with other plants for support
Light, which it must receive to do its work
Extra soil nutrients beyond what the water carries
Air that has been cooled before it reaches the leaves

items.explain: Ingenhousz showed that plants need light, not just soil and water.

items.prompt: A student says photosynthesis and cellular respiration are the same process running twice. Which correction fits best?

options.label: They are one process, but it runs only in the dark
They are one process, but it runs only inside mitochondria
They differ only in which sugar each one uses up
They are roughly opposites: one builds sugars, one breaks them down

items.explain: Photosynthesis reduces carbon dioxide to carbohydrates while cellular respiration oxidizes carbohydrates to carbon dioxide, through different reactions.

items.prompt: Why do most leaves look green?

options.label: Chlorophylls absorb red and blue light and reflect green
Chlorophylls absorb green light and reflect red and blue
Leaves make a green dye that covers the other colours up
Chloroplasts glow green while they are making oxygen

items.explain: Chlorophylls absorb the red and blue spectra of light, thus reflecting green.

items.prompt: A shade-loving plant is photosynthesizing yet gives off almost no oxygen into the air. What best explains it?

options.label: Its photosynthesis has switched to a kind that makes no oxygen
It makes oxygen only at night, when nobody measures it
It makes so little oxygen that it uses all of it itself
Its leaves soak up the oxygen made by nearby plants

items.explain: Some shade-loving plants produce such low levels of oxygen that they use all of it themselves instead of releasing it.

items.prompt: Some purple bacteria photosynthesize but give off sulfur instead of oxygen. What do they split in place of water?

options.label: Carbon dioxide gas
Hydrogen sulfide gas
Sugar from storage
Nitrogen from the air

items.explain: Some bacteria use bacteriochlorophyll to split hydrogen sulfide instead of water, releasing sulfur instead of oxygen.

items.prompt: The light reactions of photosynthesis make NADPH and ATP. What happens to these products next?

options.label: They are given off as waste once the light fades
They stay unchanged in the cell as a store for later
They are used to split water and release more oxygen
They power the capture and reduction of carbon dioxide

items.explain: The light-independent reactions use the NADPH and ATP to capture and reduce carbon dioxide into carbohydrates.
